back: To fail to use an opportunity to enjoy or get something.
To start doing something new or different (e.g., in business).
To be full of a particular feeling (e.g., excitement).
To gradually become less strong or loud (e.g., a noise).
To get rid of or abolish something.
To use something for help when other things have failed.
To become so involved in something that you cannot make progress.
To avoid talking about something unpleasant or to say as little as possible.
To be as good as expected or needed (e.g., standards).
To think carefully about something for a period of time.
To gradually stop using or providing something.
To make something seem less important than it really is.
To succeed in a very difficult situation or recover from illness.
To experience a difficulty or problem.
To choose one person or thing from a group for special attention.
